main_text.p: Rectus planus angulus, est utręq; contiguorum angulorum, quos recta linea rectæ insistens inter se fecerit æquales, græce γωνία εὐθεῖα ἐπίπεδος εὐθύγραμμος.
Sphæricus rectus, γωνία σφαιρικὴ εὐθεῖα, est utręq; angulorum contiguorum, quos περιφέρεια unius Circuli peripheriæ ulterius insistens æquales fecerit.
Obtusus angulus, ἀμβλεῖα γωνία, recto maior est.
Acutus, ὀξεῖα γωνία, recto minor est.
Obseruent studiosi & discrimen horum quatuor angulorum, quorum mentio fit frequenter.

αἱ ἐφεξῆς vocantur anguli contimui, quos recta linea non secta, sed altero terminorum extremorum secans aliam rectam, aut rectos & inter se æquales, aut obliquos & inter se inæquales, duobus vero rectis æquales efficit.

page.notes: The Greek words in the four short lines and the Greek terms in the paragraphs are only partly legible on the scan; they are transcribed as best read. Line "αἱ ἡμιορυφιῶν" and "αἱ γωνιαλάξ" and "αἱ ἀπ᾽ γνωστίων" are doubtful and should be checked against the original. The final line "αἱ" is a signature mark.
